name: shadcn/ui
summary: Composable, accessible components with thoughtful defaults. Build your own component library with code you can customize, extend, and make your own.

agent_entrypoints.what: Agent-oriented map of the docs. Start here to learn install flow, conventions, and what exists.
Machine-readable list of every registry item with per-item docs, API and example links. Use it to answer 'does a component for X exist' without guessing.
The actual source of one component for one style, e.g. .../new-york-v4/button.json. Returns the files you would copy in.
The full color scale set. Use for building a theme rather than inventing hex values.

shadcn/ui's own skill for AI assistants. It reads the project's components.json and supplies the framework, aliases, installed components, icon and base library, so generated code matches the project. Install it with the skills CLI when the user wants it permanently.
Community registries built into the CLI. Check here before concluding a component does not exist - the core registry is not the whole ecosystem.
Installs a component into the user's project. Prefer this over pasting code you generated.

use_when: The project is React-flavoured and uses Tailwind, and you need real components fast.
You want to own the component source rather than depend on a black-box package.
You need an accessible primitive (dialog, combobox, popover) and hand-rolling one would be a mistake.
You need a coherent theme and want token values that already work in light and dark.
You are building your own component library or internal registry, not just consuming components.
avoid_when: The project is not React-based - the registry assumes React component files.
The team wants a batteries-included library it never has to maintain; here the code becomes yours.

baseline.description: Composable, accessible components with thoughtful defaults. Build your own component library with code you can customize, extend, and make your own.
